public_rationale: Minerva's paper (June 2022) did test multiplication by number of digits, using 500 random questions per setting (Appendix H, Figure 8). But the results appear only as a plotted curve, with accuracy against digits in the answer. No sentence in the paper gives a 4-digit multiplication figure. A 2023 paper summarizing that figure says Minerva cannot do any multiplication 'of numbers with more than seven digits'. A 4x4-digit product has 7 or 8 digits, so this fits near-total failure. But the wording is ambiguous and does not cover 7-digit answers. The claim is plausible and broadly in line with the evidence, but no quotable source states that Minerva fails altogether on 4-digit multiplication. So I cannot score it supported or contradicted.
limitations: The decisive data exist only in a figure that the text tools cannot read.
The secondary summary may have read the figure differently from the speaker.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Minerva, despite immense training data and apparent two-digit arithmetic ability, fails altogether on 4-digit multiplication.

statement.excerpt: Minerva, for example, is trained on an immense amount of data, and ostensibly captures two-digit arithmetic, but it fails altogether on 4-digit multiplication,

from_speaker: trained on an immense amount of data
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in published evaluations, Minerva does well on two-digit arithmetic but gets near-zero accuracy when multiplying two 4-digit numbers.
'Fails altogether' means accuracy at or near zero, not just lower accuracy.
Target period: from Minerva's public evaluation (June 2022) to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: A published evaluation shows Minerva's accuracy on 4-digit by 4-digit multiplication at or near zero, while two-digit arithmetic is high.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A published evaluation shows Minerva gets a clearly non-trivial share of 4-digit multiplications right (for example well above 10%).
